scoreMetaDescription: Free online sheet music editor, no sign-up: write notes, rests, measures, clef and key signature on the staff right in your browser, with nothing to install, and download your score as PDF or MusicXML.
scoreSeoH1: Free online sheet music editor, no sign-up
scoreAboutLead: Write your score straight onto the staff: pick a note value, click where the note goes, done. It is free, runs in your browser and needs no account or install.
scoreShortcutsIntro: Press a figure’s key to pick it, then click on the staff to place it. Press A to deselect the current tool. With figures selected, Shift+D duplicates them right after the last selected one, carrying on into the following measures. Shift+↑ or Shift+↓ duplicates the selection a diatonic third above or below, in a separate voice at the same time. The copy stays selected; use ↑ and ↓ to adjust its pitch. These are the keys:
scoreShortcutsLinks: With two notes selected, press <kbd>(</kbd> or <kbd>)</kbd> to add or remove a tie or slur, if the notes can be linked. This is the same action as the contextual tie button. The shortcut follows the character: use whichever combination types the parenthesis on your keyboard, on any operating system.
scoreDotBody: Click a note to add a dot; click again for a double dot, and once more to remove it.
scoreBarBody: Click a single, double or repeat barline to highlight it in yellow, then press Delete to remove it.
scoreTabEditBody: Click a number in the tab and type the new fret; your fingering is saved and the staff does not change.
scoreTabMoveBody: Drag a number to another string or another beat and drop it wherever you want.
scoreFeaturesH2: What you can do with the editor
scoreFeatures: Notes and rests: from whole to thirty-second notes, with dots and accidentals (sharps, flats and naturals).
Measures: pick the time signature (4/4, 3/4, 6/8…) and the editor will not let a measure overflow.
Clef and key signature: treble, bass and C clefs, and any key signature from C♭ to C♯.
Special barlines: double barlines, repeat signs and guitar barre marks.
Settings: piano with a grand staff or guitar with tablature, tempo in the score and the MIDI, and colors to tell voices apart.
Download: export the score as a PDF to print, or as MusicXML to open in MuseScore, Finale, Sibelius or Dorico.
Autosave: your score is kept in your browser, so you can pick it up another day.
scoreHowH2: How to write sheet music online
scoreHow: Type the title and the composer above the score.
Choose a note value or a rest in the toolbar.
Click on the staff to place each note; they group into measures on their own.
Adjust the clef, key signature and barlines if needed.
Download the score as PDF or MusicXML.
scoreFaq: Is it really free to write sheet music here?
Yes. The editor is free, with no usage limits and no account.
Do I need to sign up or install anything?
No. It works in any modern browser on a computer, tablet or phone. Your score is saved in your own browser.
PDF, to print or share, and MusicXML, the standard format that MuseScore, Finale, Sibelius and Dorico open.
Yes. In Settings choose Guitar and you get the guitar treble clef (an octave lower), tablature, repeat signs and barre marks. For piano, the other instrument, every system is a grand staff.

tutorials.metaTitle: Tutorials · Partitura, free online sheet music editor
tutorials.metaDescription: Learn to use the free online sheet music editor, no sign-up, step by step with animations: notes and rests, editing, measures, repeats, dynamics, guitar tablature and files.
tutorials.intro: Partitura is a score editor that runs right in your browser. Here is what is worth knowing before you start.

cards.title: Online, nothing to install
cards.text: Unlike MuseScore, Sibelius, Dorico and other desktop programs, there is nothing to download or install: it runs in the browser, on any computer.

cards.title: No sign-up
cards.text: There is no account to create and no login: open the page and start writing, unlike Noteflight or Flat.io.

cards.title: As many scores as you like
cards.text: You can keep several scores open at once, each in its own tab.

cards.title: Saved in your browser
cards.text: Everything is saved on your device as you write. Nothing is uploaded to any server. To keep or share a score, export it from the menu.

cards.title: Free and ad-free
cards.text: The site is free and has no advertising: no ads or trackers to distract you.

cards.title: Built to be intuitive
cards.text: We work hard to make the interface clear without explanations. Even so, the menu on the left has tutorials for every feature and a guide with all the keyboard shortcuts.

welcome.start: If this is your first time, start with “Getting started” in the menu on the left.

start: How to write your first score online.
features: Notes, measures, clef, key signature, barlines and downloads.
shortcuts: The key for every note, rest and accidental.
dots: Add, double or remove a dot by clicking the note.
delete-barline: Select a barline and remove it.
edit-tab: Change a note’s fret without touching the staff.
move-tab: Move a number and change its string
Drag a number or use Shift+↑/↓ to play the same sound on another string.
faq: Free use, download formats and guitar.
notes-rests: Pick a figure, click the staff and keep writing.
accidentals: Alter a note with one key and one click.
select-move: Pick one or several figures and move them without rewriting.
copy: Repeat a motif in a couple of keystrokes.
tuplets: Turn consecutive figures into a triplet, a quintuplet and more.
ties: Join two notes with a tie or group eighth notes with a beam.
signatures: Change the meter, clef or key anywhere in the score.
measures: Build the structure of the score measure by measure.
repeats: Repeat barlines, da capo, segno and endings.
tab-toggle: A tab under every system, with the fingering already worked out.
barre: Mark a barre and its fret over the notes it covers.
settings: Piano or guitar, tempo, and which tool groups to show.
files: Open a MusicXML or MIDI file and download your score as PDF, MusicXML or MIDI.
scores: Work on several scores at once; everything saves itself in your browser.
voices: Duplicate a melody above or below and edit each line independently.
playback: Play piano or guitar, start at a measure and listen to voices separately.
patterns: Save a motif and reuse its intervals or just its rhythm.
chords: Write names above the staff and explore fingerings and variants.
lyrics: Write syllables under the notes, paste a whole lyric, move them and merge them.

steps: Pick a figure in the palette or press its key: <kbd>1</kbd> (32nd) to <kbd>6</kbd> (whole) for notes, and <kbd>Q</kbd> to <kbd>Y</kbd> for rests.
Click the staff: the height of the click is the pitch and the horizontal position is the time. You can also drag the figure from the palette to its place.

To prepend a note, place it to the left of the first figure in the measure, leaving a gap between them: the figures in the nearest voice shift to make room. Placing it on the same column starts it at the same time in another voice.

To insert a note or rest between figures, place it in the gap between two columns: it is inserted before the right column in the voice nearest the chosen pitch. The following figures shift if they fit in the measure.
The tool stays active after each figure, so you can write a whole phrase without picking it again. Eighth notes and shorter ones beam themselves.
Press <kbd>A</kbd> or <kbd>Esc</kbd> to drop the tool and go back to selecting figures.
To fill an empty measure with rests, click to select it and press <kbd>Tab</kbd>. The largest values that complete its duration are used; in piano mode, only the selected staff is filled.
notes-rests.tip: If a figure does not fit in what is left of the measure, the editor tells you and does not place it.

steps: Press <kbd>S</kbd> for a sharp, <kbd>B</kbd> for a flat or <kbd>C</kbd> for a natural. They are in the palette too.
Click the note you want to alter: the sign appears to its left.
You can also select a note first, then press <kbd>S</kbd>, <kbd>B</kbd> or <kbd>C</kbd>: the accidental applies directly to the selection without another click.
Dots work the same way: press <kbd>P</kbd> and click the note, or just click the note with no tool in hand: dot, double dot, none.
Click a figure to select it. <kbd>Shift</kbd>, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> adds more. Dragging from an empty spot on the staff encloses them in a rectangle.
<kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> raise or lower the selection by one staff step; <kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> move to the next figure. You can also drag the figures elsewhere.

Use <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>←</kbd>/<kbd>→</kbd> to extend the selection to neighboring figures. <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>↑</kbd>/<kbd>↓</kbd> creates a copy in another voice, a diatonic third above or below at the same time; the copies stay selected.
<kbd>Delete</kbd> or <kbd>Backspace</kbd> removes them. <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Z</kbd> undoes the last change and <kbd>Esc</kbd> clears the selection.
Select one or more figures and press <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>D</kbd>: they are copied right after the last selected one, carrying on into the measures that follow.

To bring them somewhere else, copy with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd>, click the destination measure and paste with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd>. It works between open scores too.

To write a second voice, use <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>↑</kbd>/<kbd>↓</kbd>: the copy sits a diatonic third above or below with the same timing and durations. Release Shift and adjust its pitch with the arrows. This works in either piano staff.

Copying, pasting and duplicating preserve ties and slurs when both ends are included. To reuse a motif at other pitches or keep only its rhythm, save it to the pattern library with <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>S</kbd>.
copy.tip: Hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> while pasting to paste only the figures, without clef, key or meter changes.

steps: Select 2 to 9 consecutive figures of the same value, for example three eighth notes.
A menu appears over the selection with the group that matches how many there are: triplet, duplet, quadruplet, quintuplet, sextuplet, septuplet, octuplet or nonuplet.
Pick the group: the figures shrink to fit the same time and the number shows above them.
To undo it, select the group and choose Remove triplet (or whichever applies) from the same menu.
Select two consecutive notes with Shift+click. In the menu over them choose Tie: if they sound the same a tie is drawn, otherwise a slur.
You can link consecutive notes in the same voice within a measure, or the last column of a measure with the first of the next. Both ends must be on the same staff.
To remove it, select the same notes and choose Remove tie. You can also press ( or ) to toggle the tie or slur between the selected notes, if they can be linked.
You can also click an arc directly to select it, then press <kbd>Delete</kbd> or <kbd>Backspace</kbd> to remove the tie or slur without deleting the notes.
Beams work the same way: select consecutive figures and choose Beam to join them or Unbeam to split the beam. If you do nothing, the editor groups them by the meter.
Click the meter number, the clef or the key signature spot at the start of a system.
Pick the value in the menu: meter (4/4, 3/4, 6/8…), clef (treble, guitar treble, bass, alto or tenor) or key (from C♭ to C♯). For clef and key, confirm with Apply.
The change holds from that measure until the next change, so you can switch meter or key mid-piece.
signatures.tip: If the figures you already wrote do not fit the new meter, the editor asks you to remove or move some before changing it.

steps: Click an empty part of a measure to select it: two + buttons appear at its edges to insert a measure before or after.
At the end of each system, the + and − buttons add or remove a measure. To add another system use the button under the score.
Hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> and drag a measure to move it elsewhere.
Drag a barline sideways to make a measure wider or narrower.
To delete a measure, click an empty part of it to select it and press <kbd>Delete</kbd>: the following measures move up to fill the gap.
In the palette, pick Repeat start, Repeat end or Double bar and click the measure where it goes.
For jumps, pick Da capo, Dal segno, Segno, First ending or Second ending and click the measure: the sign sits above the staff.
To delete a barline or a sign, click it to select it and press <kbd>Delete</kbd>.
In the palette pick Crescendo or Diminuendo and click the note where it starts: the hairpin runs to the end of the measure.
Click it to select it: two handles appear under its ends to widen or shorten it.
Each end has a spot for a dynamic, showing the suggested one (p → f on a crescendo). Click it to choose another, from ppp to fff, or none.
Press the TAB button in the palette: a six-string tablature appears under every system.

The first tablature shows the string names, from highest to lowest (E B G D A E in standard tuning). Click these names to choose Standard, Drop D, Double Drop D, DADGAD, Open D or Open G. The menu lists strings from lowest to highest.
Changing tuning recalculates all frets and replaces manual fingerings while preserving the staff notes. Tuning is saved with this score, and you can undo the change with Ctrl/Cmd+Z.
The editor picks the most comfortable fingering by itself: it keeps the hand in one position, avoids jumps and does not reuse a string for different notes.
The staff does not change when you touch the tablature. Press the button again to hide it.
tab-toggle.tip: The next two guides explain how to change a number or move it to another string.

steps: In the palette pick Barre and click the note where it starts (or anywhere in the measure to cover it from the beginning).
A C appears with a field for the fret: type a number from 1 to 24 and press Enter.
Drag the handles at its ends, or use <kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> on them, to change how far it reaches. Clear the number to remove the barre.

Open Settings with the cog {{icon:settings}}, the first tool in the right toolbar. Except for the pattern library, they apply to the score you are looking at, are saved with it, and can be undone with Ctrl/Cmd + Z.

Instrument: with Piano {{icon:piano}} every system is a grand staff, treble clef above and bass clef below joined by a brace, and TAB and barre are hidden. With Guitar {{icon:guitar}} there is a single staff in guitar treble clef, and the TAB button and barre appear. Switching between them deletes nothing: whatever is hidden stays saved.
Tempo: the slider goes from 20 to 300 quarter notes per minute. It is written as a metronome mark above the first measure and sets the speed of the exported MIDI. No marking removes it.

Tools: turn Repeats, Dynamics and Voices on or off to show or hide their controls in the editor toolbars. Hiding a group does not delete what you already wrote. With Voices on, each voice gets a color (1 to 4) and a legend appears to the left of the brace, where you choose which voices to color; no note is ever hidden.

Grand staff: each staff has its own notes, rests, voices and clef (the clef menu says which one it changes). Measures, key signature, time signature, barlines, repeats and tempo are shared by both. Dynamics and hairpins are written between the two.

Playback: {{icon:play}}{{icon:pause}} enable it to show play/pause to the left of the staff. It uses this score’s instrument and tempo. With Voices enabled, the selected legend numbers also filter what you hear; with none selected, all voices play.
Pattern library: opens a separate panel to save and reuse motifs with Shift+S. This preference and the patterns belong to the user and browser, rather than to each score.
The left and right toolbars and the pattern library stay within reach as you scroll; on short screens, the toolbars scroll with the page.
settings.tip: On export, piano goes into MusicXML as a single part with two staves, and in MIDI each staff plays on its own channel.

steps: Open the ☰ menu at the top right.
Load file… opens a MusicXML (.musicxml, .xml) or a MIDI (.mid) file and turns it into a new score.
Export downloads the score: PDF to print, MusicXML for MuseScore, Finale, Sibelius or Dorico, and MIDI to play it in any program.
Multi-page PDFs are numbered automatically; a single-page PDF has no page number.
Open scores are the tabs at the top. The + button creates a new empty one, and clicking a tab takes you back to the one you left.
Everything saves itself in your browser as you write: come back another day and it is all there. Nothing is uploaded to any server.
The trash button clears the score you are looking at, and asks for confirmation first.
scores.tip: Clearing your browser data loses the scores: export as MusicXML the ones you want to keep.

steps: Select a note or phrase on the staff. Extend the selection with <kbd>Shift</kbd>+click or <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>←</kbd>/<kbd>→</kbd>.

Press <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>↑</kbd> to duplicate it a diatonic third above, or <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>↓</kbd> to duplicate it below. The copies start at the same times and keep durations, dots, tuplets, and ties or slurs whose two ends are selected.

The copies stay selected. Release <kbd>Shift</kbd> and use <kbd>↑</kbd>/<kbd>↓</kbd> to adjust only their pitch. For example, duplicate below to write a diatonic third below the melody; the arrows without Shift let you adjust the interval one staff step at a time. You can also select and edit individual notes in the new line.

Duplication example: in C major, write C–D–E as quarter notes, select all three and press Shift + ↑. This adds E–F–G in another voice, at the same times as C–D–E. Using Shift + ↓ on the original phrase gives A–B–C below it. The thirds follow the key signature; they do not always span the same number of semitones.

Each selected voice gets an independent copy on the same staff. This works in either piano staff; the copy does not move to the other staff. <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Z</kbd> undoes the duplication.

Enable Voices in settings to show the color legend on the left. Select the voice numbers to color; the other figures stay visible. With Playback enabled too, you can listen only to the selected voices.

Correcting the voice of existing notes: automatic voice calculation can fail, for example when two lines cross or share a rhythm. If a melody note ends up in the accompaniment voice, you can reassign it without duplicating it or changing its pitch, onset or duration.

Enable Voices in settings and activate the destination voice number in the legend. Select the notes to correct, even a single note, and choose Assign notes to voice N in the menu beside the selection, using the corresponding number. For example, if an E in the melody ends up in voice 2, activate voice 1, select that E and choose Assign notes to voice 1. Only the selected notes are reassigned; the others keep their voices.

The assignment option appears only for voices active in the legend, when at least one selected figure belongs to another voice and the change can preserve the rhythm. If it is missing, check these conditions and that the destination voice has no incompatible overlapping figures. <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Z</kbd> undoes the reassignment.
voices.tip: Duplication is rejected if a note already exists at that pitch and time, the pitch range or 16-voice limit is exceeded, or timing cannot be preserved. In tablature, Shift+↑/↓ changes strings without duplicating: select notes on the staff to create voices.

steps: Open the Settings gear {{icon:settings}} and enable Playback under Tools. A play button appears to the left of the staff, above the voice legend.

Choose Piano {{icon:piano}} or Guitar {{icon:guitar}} and set the tempo. The written notes play with a piano or nylon guitar sound; both staves play in piano mode. You may see Loading sounds… the first time.

Press {{icon:play}} Play or the space bar. A vertical bar follows the music and moves to the next system. Playback starts at the last position you clicked, on a figure or in empty space, even after deselecting. With no previous click, it starts at the beginning. Clicking empty space repositions the line and keeps it visible to mark that position. During playback, click to jump there immediately.
Press {{icon:pause}} Pause or the space bar to keep your position, then play again to continue. If you click another position while paused, playback starts there.

To hear a line separately, enable Voices and select its numbers in the legend: the filter applies to both staves. With no voices selected, all voices play. Changing this selection stops playback and resets its position.
Editing the music, switching scores or hiding the page stops playback and resets its position. Press play again when you want to hear the result.
playback.tip: The voice filter only affects playback in the editor: exported MIDI includes all voices. MIDI also uses the selected tempo.

steps: Enable Pattern library in Settings. The Patterns panel opens to the left of the editor. This is your preference and stays enabled when you switch scores.

Select figures from a single staff and press <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>S</kbd>. With no figures selected, click a measure and use the same shortcut to save it. Saving the same pattern again does not add a duplicate.

Each pattern shows scale degrees and figures. Drag the left area, with the degrees, onto the staff: the first note takes the destination pitch and the others keep their distance in scale steps. Ghost figures preview the result.
Drag the right area, with the figures, to apply only the rhythm: all notes use the same pitch. Rests, durations, dots, tuplets, and internal ties and slurs are preserved.
You can also select a measure and click either area: the pattern starts at the beginning of the measure on the middle line. If it does not fit, the editor does not apply it.
Use Remove pattern to delete an item from the library. The library keeps up to 60 patterns and is available across scores in this browser.
patterns.tip: Patterns store relationships between notes, not the original key, accidentals or voices. The library is local and is not included when you export a score; clearing site data also clears the library.

steps: Choose Guitar in settings and activate the Am tool in the palette. Place it on the note where the chord starts: a name field appears.
Type a name, such as Am, and press Enter or leave the field to save. Esc or an empty field cancels. The tool deactivates after you write the chord.
Click an existing name to open its panel: edit it, remove it or view its fingering diagram. The variant controls show other positions for the same chord and save your choice.
If no fingering is available for a name, the name stays written and the panel tells you. Use the search field to find a chord in the dictionary.
Drag a name to another beat or measure: the underlined area marks the destination. Only one chord is allowed at each time; it cannot move onto another chord.
To delete several names together, drag a selection rectangle around them and press <kbd>Delete</kbd> or <kbd>Backspace</kbd>. Undo changes with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Z</kbd>.
chords.tip: Chord names appear above the staff and in PDF exports. The diagram is a reference: writing a chord name does not add its notes to the staff or make them sound during playback.

steps: With the Lyrics tool {{icon:lyric}}, in the right toolbar, place the cursor over the note where the syllable starts: a field opens under the staff. If you can't see the tool, turn on Lyrics in the settings {{icon:settings}}. With guitar and piano the lyric goes under the top staff; with Voices, under each staff.

Type the syllable and press <kbd>Space</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd>: it is saved and the field jumps to the next note of the same staff, even in another measure. <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd> goes back, <kbd>Enter</kbd> saves and closes, <kbd>Esc</kbd> cancels and leaving it empty deletes the syllable. Rests are skipped.

No hyphens are drawn between one note and the next: each syllable appears alone under its note. When two syllables are sung on a single sound, type them with a hyphen or with Shift + Space (a space inside the same syllable, without moving to the next note): the hyphen becomes a space and a small tie is drawn between the two, so en-a or en a show as en‿a under one note.

To load a whole lyric, paste it with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd> inside the field. It is split into syllables (Spanish) and spread one per note from the note that has the field, across measures. Line breaks are ignored, so you can paste a paragraph or several lines, and extra spaces are trimmed. What was already written on those notes is overwritten; if there aren't enough notes, the editor says how many syllables were left out.

A note tied to the previous one takes no syllable: the sound is held, not struck again. The tool doesn't open the field on it, Space and pasting skip it and a syllable never lands there. So in Can⌒to, the syllable to goes on the next note that is struck. A slur between different pitches doesn't count: those notes are struck and take a syllable.

If you tie a note that already had a syllable, the syllable is kept but no longer drawn or exported; remove the tie and it comes back. To edit a written syllable, click it; to remove it, leave the field empty or focus it and press <kbd>Delete</kbd> or <kbd>Backspace</kbd>.

As with chords, you can drag a syllable to another note: the underlined zone marks the destination. It fixes an offset without retyping. It only moves within the same staff and to a free note; a rest, a tied note or a note that already has a syllable is refused.

To merge syllables, select their notes: drag a selection rectangle over them or add each one with Shift + click on the syllable (or Ctrl/Cmd + click). They must be in the same staff and at least two must have a syllable. The menu next to the selection offers Merge syllables {{icon:merge}}.

When merged, the first one keeps its place and takes the text of all of them, joined with spaces: Can and to become Can to under the first note. The following syllables move one place to the left to fill the freed one, across measures, and the selection is cleared.

With three or more syllables the shift follows: as many places are freed as syllables were added minus one, and every later syllable moves up by that amount. Gaps that already existed between syllables are kept, and tied notes are still skipped. If the merged text is longer than the maximum length of a syllable, the editor says so and changes nothing.

Everything can be undone with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Z</kbd>. The lyric is saved with the score and appears in the PDF and in MusicXML; it is not exported to MIDI, not imported from MusicXML and doesn't travel on the clipboard when copying notes.
lyrics.tip: Lyrics are a Pro feature: the tool appears when the address ends in #pro and can be hidden with the Lyrics checkbox in the settings without deleting anything. Hidden syllables are still drawn and exported, but can no longer be edited.

steps: Drag a number in the tablature to another string or beat and drop it wherever you want.
To play the same sound on another string, click the number of the note you want to change.

Press <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>↓</kbd> (or <kbd>↑</kbd>): the editor looks for the next fingering of that note on the following strings and adjusts the fret so it sounds the same. Press again to move on to the next string, as long as the fret stays within the maximum.
move-tab.tip: Only the fingering changes: the note on the staff and the sound stay the same.

shortcutSections: Press a figure’s key to pick it, then click on the staff to place it.
Press <kbd>A</kbd> to deselect the current tool.
To fill an empty measure with rests, select it with a click and press <kbd>Tab</kbd>. On piano, only the chosen staff is filled.
If the measure already has figures, <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Tab</kbd> completes what each voice is missing with rests.
With figures selected, <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>D</kbd> duplicates them right after the last selected one, carrying on into the following measures.
<kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>↑</kbd> or <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>↓</kbd> duplicates the selection a diatonic third above or below, in a separate voice at the same time.
The copy stays selected; use <kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> to adjust its pitch.

With two notes selected, press <kbd>(</kbd> or <kbd>)</kbd> to add or remove a tie or slur, if the notes can be linked. This is the same action as the contextual tie button. The shortcut follows the character: use whichever combination types the parenthesis on your keyboard, on any operating system.

<kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> move to the neighbouring figure; <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>←</kbd> or <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>→</kbd> extend the selection. <kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> raise or lower the selection one step.
<kbd>Delete</kbd> or <kbd>Backspace</kbd> remove the selected figures, or the chosen measure or barline. <kbd>Esc</kbd> clears the selection.

<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> copies the selected figures; click the destination measure and paste with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd>. Hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> while pasting to leave out the meter, clef and key signature.
With the pattern library turned on in the settings, <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>S</kbd> saves the chosen figures as a pattern or, with none chosen, the chosen measure.
With playback turned on in the settings, the <kbd>space bar</kbd> toggles play and pause.

terms.metaDescription: Terms of use for Partitura, the free online score editor with no sign-up: using the service, your scores, intellectual property and liability.
sections: By using Partitura you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, do not use the service.
Partitura is a free score editor that runs in your browser. No sign-up is needed. We may change, suspend or remove features at any time, with or without notice.

The scores you write are stored only in your browser (local storage) and are not sent to any server. Because we hold no copy, we cannot recover them: clearing your browser data or switching devices loses them. Export your work (PDF, MusicXML or MIDI) to keep it. Partitura is in its beta phase: we are not responsible for any loss of data during this phase, nor if you clear your browser cache or data.

Your compositions and arrangements are yours; we only provide the tool to write them. You are responsible for having the rights to any content you load or transcribe, such as copyrighted works by others. The design, code and brand of Partitura belong to their authors; the third-party software we use keeps its own licences.
Please do not use the service for unlawful activity, to try to compromise or overload it, or to infringe the rights of others.

Partitura is provided "as is" and "as available", without warranties of any kind. We do not promise that it is error-free, that it will run without interruption, or that its output is fit for a particular purpose, such as professional engraving or printing.
To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for loss of data, work or income, or for any other damage arising from using the service or being unable to use it.
We may update these terms. The date above shows the latest revision; continuing to use Partitura after a change means you accept it.
